findings: requested_top_k is the already validated caller request; returned_count counts exactly the records shown in that result; limit_reached is true exactly when the shown count equals the requested cap. No total, has_more or unobserved-record assertion is made.

The generic public description explicitly states that reaching the cap neither establishes additional records nor guarantees completeness. The description contains no task answer, scenario-specific instruction or model action restriction.

Independent AST comparison confirms the contract changes only the retrieve description. Policy, argument schemas, action parser, task allowlists, budgets and validation code are byte-equivalent in AST.

Independent AST comparison confirms the gateway changes only the three public response keys. Removing those keys makes the complete gateway module AST identical to the base. Retrieval query, top_k, trusted scope, effective time, receipt matching, record data, authority handling and write behavior are unchanged.

Four added cases exercise a capped result, exactly all eligible records at the cap, a result below the cap and an empty scoped result. They prove one unchanged scoped read, unchanged raw report and journal, preservation of exact observed records/references, and absence of unshown memory text or scope metadata. An existing write test additionally checks its response remains records-only.

Independent controls also exercise results without a complete owned receipt, at and below the cap: metadata counts public records even while observed_records is empty and record_ref remains null. A foreign-scope adapter result still fails before any public result is returned.
No source file outside the three reviewed paths differs from the base commit. Source hashes were checked after independent execution.
